1. Eczema 1677.name: Eczema
1. Eczema 1677.description: Eczema is a common condition that causes dry, itchy, inflamed, and irritated skin patches. It can flare periodically and is not contagious.
symptoms: Dry, sensitive skin
Intense itching (pruritus)
Red to brownish-gray patches
Small raised bumps that may leak fluid when scratched
Cracked, scaly skin
common_triggers: Allergens like pollen or pet dander
1. Eczema 1677.when_to_see_doctor: Seek evaluation if the rash is intensely painful, shows signs of bacterial infection (pus, yellow crusting), or interferes with sleep.
care_tips: Moisturize frequently with fragrance-free ointments
Take short, lukewarm showers
Avoid known irritants and wear soft, breathable cotton fabrics

10. Warts Molluscum and other Viral Infe.name: Viral Infections (Warts & Molluscum)
10. Warts Molluscum and other Viral Infe.description: Skin conditions caused by viral infections, including common warts, plantar warts, and dome-shaped molluscum contagiosum bumps with central dimples.
symptoms: Small, fleshy, grainy bumps
Rough to touch
Flesh-colored, white, or pink firm lesions
Central indentation (umbilication) in molluscum
10. Warts Molluscum and other Viral Infe.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if lesions are painful, spreading rapidly, bleeding, or located on sensitive areas.
care_tips: Do not scratch, pick, or shave over lesions to prevent spreading
Keep hands clean and dry
Avoid sharing personal hygiene items

2. Melanoma 15.75k.name: Melanoma
2. Melanoma 15.75k.description: Melanoma is the most serious form of skin cancer, arising from pigment-producing melanocytes. Early detection and immediate clinical biopsy are critical.
symptoms: Asymmetrical mole (ABCDE rule)
Irregular, scalloped or notched border
Varied shades of brown, black, blue, red, or white
Diameter larger than 6mm (pencil eraser size)
Evolving size, shape, color, or new itching/bleeding
common_triggers: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sun exposure or tanning beds
Fair skin, light hair, or history of blistering sunburns
2. Melanoma 15.75k.when_to_see_doctor: IMMEDIATE medical consultation with a dermatologist or oncologist is strongly recommended for any suspicious mole.
care_tips: Perform regular full-body skin self-exams
Wear broad-spectrum SPF 30+ sunscreen daily
Avoid peak sun hours and tanning beds

3. Atopic Dermatitis - 1.25k.name: Atopic Dermatitis
3. Atopic Dermatitis - 1.25k.description: A chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease commonly associated with a genetic predisposition to allergic rhinitis, asthma, or food allergies.
symptoms: Severe itching, often worse at night
Thickened, lichenified skin from repeated scratching
Erythematous papules and plaques in skin creases (elbows, behind knees)
3. Atopic Dermatitis - 1.25k.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a dermatologist if over-the-counter moisturizers fail to provide relief or if signs of secondary infection appear.
care_tips: Apply thick emollient creams immediately after bathing
Use mild, soap-free cleansers
Manage stress and maintain optimal indoor humidity

4. Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) 3323.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC)
4. Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) 3323.description: The most common form of skin cancer. It grows slowly and rarely metastasizes to distant sites, but can cause extensive local tissue destruction if untreated.
symptoms: Pearly or waxy translucent bump with visible tiny blood vessels (telangiectasias)
Flat, firm, pale or yellow scar-like area
Persistent non-healing sore that bleeds, oozes, or crusts
Elevated pink growth with a central depression
common_triggers: Fair skin with high susceptibility to sunburn
4. Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) 3323.when_to_see_doctor: Prompt evaluation by a dermatologist is recommended for biopsy and surgical or topical removal.
care_tips: Protect face, ears, neck, and scalp with wide-brimmed hats
Apply sunscreen rigorously
Schedule regular dermatological screenings

5. Melanocytic Nevi (NV) - 7970.name: Melanocytic Nevi (Common Mole)
5. Melanocytic Nevi (NV) - 7970.description: Common benign growths composed of melanocytes. Most adults have between 10 and 40 moles, which are generally harmless.
symptoms: Evenly pigmented round or oval spot
Clear, well-defined border
Uniform tan, brown, or black color
Stable size typically under 6mm
common_triggers: Sun exposure during childhood and adolescence
5. Melanocytic Nevi (NV) - 7970.when_to_see_doctor: Monitor with the ABCDE criteria; consult a physician if any mole changes in size, shape, color, or starts itching or bleeding.
care_tips: Take regular photos of existing moles to track changes
Use sun protection to prevent UV damage

6. Benign Keratosis-like Lesions (BKL) 2.name: Benign Keratosis
6. Benign Keratosis-like Lesions (BKL) 2.description: Non-cancerous skin lesions encompassing sun spots (solar lentigines) and lichen planus-like keratosis, frequently appearing in sun-exposed areas of older adults.
symptoms: Flat or slightly raised macules or thin plaques
Tan, brown, reddish or grayish coloration
Sharply demarcated borders
6. Benign Keratosis-like Lesions (BKL) 2.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a healthcare provider if a lesion looks atypical, grows rapidly, or resembles melanoma.
care_tips: Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen
Gentle skin hygiene
Routine clinical skin checks

7. Psoriasis pictures Lichen Planus and.name: Psoriasis & Lichen Planus
7. Psoriasis pictures Lichen Planus and.description: Immune-mediated dermatological conditions where rapid skin cell turnover produces thick, silvery-scaled plaques or violaceous polygonal itchy papules.
symptoms: Raised red patches covered with thick, silvery scales (Psoriasis)
Itchy, flat-topped purple bumps (Lichen Planus)
Dry, cracked skin that may bleed
Pitted or discolored nails
7. Psoriasis pictures Lichen Planus and.when_to_see_doctor: See a dermatologist for systemic, biologic, or targeted topical therapies, especially if joint pain (psoriatic arthritis) is present.
care_tips: Keep skin moisturized
Controlled sunlight exposure under doctor advice
Avoid smoking and excessive alcohol

8. Seborrheic Keratoses and other Benign.name: Seborrheic Keratosis
8. Seborrheic Keratoses and other Benign.description: One of the most common non-cancerous skin growths in older adults. They often appear 'pasted on' or waxy.
symptoms: Round or oval growths with a waxy, scaly, or 'stuck-on' appearance
Tan, brown, or black color
Slightly raised with a velvety to verrucous surface
8. Seborrheic Keratoses and other Benign.when_to_see_doctor: Check with a doctor if the growth becomes inflamed from clothing friction, bleeds, or is difficult to distinguish from melanoma.
care_tips: Avoid scratching or picking at growths
Cryotherapy or curettage can be performed by a clinician if irritated

9. Tinea Ringworm Candidiasis and other.name: Fungal Infections (Tinea & Candidiasis)
9. Tinea Ringworm Candidiasis and other.description: Fungal infections of the outer skin layers (such as ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, or candidal intertrigo).
symptoms: Circular rash with raised, red, scaly edges and clearer center (ringworm)
Intense itching, burning, or stinging
Cracking, peeling skin in moist folds or between toes
Red, macerated patches with satellite pustules
9. Tinea Ringworm Candidiasis and other.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical attention if the infection does not improve after 2 weeks of antifungal treatment or spreads to the scalp or nails.
care_tips: Keep infected areas thoroughly clean and dry
Use prescribed or OTC antifungal creams as directed
Wear loose, breathable footwear and clothing

11. Normal Skin.name: Normal / Healthy Skin
11. Normal Skin.description: No visible signs of the supported skin conditions were detected in this image. The skin appears normal with intact cutaneous barrier function.
symptoms: Smooth, intact cutaneous surface
Even pigmentation without suspicious focal macules
Absence of suspicious erythematous patches, plaques, scaling, or ulcerations
11. Normal Skin.when_to_see_doctor: Continue routine preventive skin self-examinations. Consult a certified dermatologist if you notice any new, changing, itching, or bleeding spots.
care_tips: Maintain daily skin barrier moisturization
Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen when exposed to sunlight
Avoid harsh chemical abrasives or excessive scrubbing
